                                              CGL: Advancing Continual GUI Learning via Reinforcement Fine-Tuning

                                                                      *                          *                                                                                   *
                                               Zhenquan Yao1 , Zitong Huang1 , Yihan Zeng2† , Jianhua Han2 , Hang Xu2 , Chun-Mei Feng3

                                                                      Abstract
                                        Graphical User Interface (GUI) Agents, benefiting from
                                        recent advances in multimodal large language models
                                        (MLLM), have achieved significant development. However,
                                        due to the frequent updates of GUI applications, adapt-
                                        ing to new tasks without forgetting old tasks in GUI con-
                                        tinual learning remains an open problem. In this work,
                                        we reveal that while Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) facili-
                                        tates fast adaptation, it often triggers knowledge overwrit-
                                        ing, whereas Reinforcement Learning (RL) demonstrates an
                                        inherent resilience that shields prior interaction logic from
                                        erasure. Based on this insight, we propose a Continual
                                        GUI Learning (CGL) framework that dynamically balances
                                        adaptation efficiency and skill retention by enhancing the
                                        synergy between SFT and RL. Specifically, we introduce an
                                        SFT proportion adjustment mechanism guided by policy en-
                                        tropy to dynamically control the weight allocation between
                                        the SFT and RL training phases. To resolve explicit gradi-
                                        ent interference, we further develop a specialized gradient                      Figure 1. Overview of Continual GUI Learning (CGL). (a) GUI
                                        surgery strategy. By projecting exploratory SFT gradients                        environments evolve as new app categories emerge, causing static
                                        onto GRPO-based anchor gradients, our method explicitly                          GUI agents to misalign with the real world. (b) Existing paradigms
                                        clips the components of SFT gradients that conflict with                         struggle to balance stability in legacy tasks and plasticity in novel
                                        GRPO. On top of that, we establish an AndroidControl-CL                          task accuracy. (c) Our CGL framework achieves balanced adapta-
                                        benchmark, which divides GUI applications into distinct                          tion and retention.
                                        task groups to effectively simulate and evaluate the per-
                                        formance of continual GUI learning. Experimental results                         have demonstrated significant potential in automating com-
                                        demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed CGL frame-                         plex interactions within software ecosystems [2, 9, 26, 28,
                                        work across continual learning scenarios. The benchmark,                         29, 33]. By interpreting visual semantics and executing
                                        code, and model will be made publicly available.                                 hierarchical action sequences, these agents bridge the gap
                                                                                                                         between high-level user intent and low-level interface exe-
                                                                                                                         cution. However, the prevailing training paradigm remains
                                        1. Introduction                                                                  largely static, standing in stark contrast to the highly dy-
                                                                                                                         namic evolution of real-world GUI environments [6, 22, 33,

the aggressive gradient updates in SFT forcibly pull the              Traditional continual learning methods are mainly catego-
model parameters toward the manifold of the new task,                 rized into three types [25]: Regularization-based methods

tinct inherent resilience. It preserves broader behavioral di-        protect old-task parameters; they are lightweight but face
versity, allowing the agent to optimize for rewards without           challenges in importance measurement and loss weight bal-
entirely erasing the underlying interaction logic. Neverthe-          ancing. Dynamic Architecture methods [34, 41] freeze old
less, this stability is attained at the expense of high sample        parameters and add task-specific sub-networks, which the-
complexity, resulting in protracted adaptation speeds in un-          oretically avoid forgetting but lead to linear model size ex-
familiar environments that fail to meet real-world efficiency         pansion with increasing tasks. Rehearsal methods [15, 24]
requirements.                                                         use memory buffers to mix old and new task data during

synergistic mechanism encompassing conflict quantifica-               learning faces unique challenges like maintaining cross-
tion and gradient rectification to reconcile the trade-off be-        modal alignment. Core solutions include Multi-Modal Re-
tween adaptation efficiency and skill retention. Specifi-             play (MMRE) [4, 12, 17, 30, 44]: it adopts explicit or im-
cally, we first introduce Error-Aware Routing to dynami-              plicit replay, where explicit replay stores old image-text

sition with retention, we develop Entropy-Regulated Tun-              pseudo-data quality respectively. Cross-Modal Regulariza-
ing, which modulates the weight of the supervised objective           tion (CREG) [11, 42, 46] adds constraint terms to retain
based on real-time policy uncertainty. Furthermore, we im-            old cross-modal associations, and its key issue is balancing
plement Gradient Surgery to project exploratory SFT gradi-            constraint intensity. Parameter-Efficient Adaptation (PEA)
ents onto a conflict-free subspace defined by GRPO-based              [7, 10, 14, 19] uses lightweight modules without modifying
anchor gradients, effectively resolving parameter-level in-           core parameters to preserve zero-shot capability, but may
terference between the two objectives. This projection pro-           struggle with complex tasks due to limited adjustable pa-
cess enables selective filtering of update directions, preserv-       rameters. Recent work [16] proposes a rollout-based In-

                                                                  2
                                                                              Within each application ak,m ∈ Ak , the agent interacts
                                                                          through trajectories. A trajectory τ = (I, {vt , at }Tt=1 ) con-
                                                                          sists of:
                                                                          • a natural language instruction I specifying the target goal,
                                                                          • a sequence of visual observations vt ∈ RH×W ×C repre-
                                                                            senting GUI screenshots at timestep t,
                                                                          • a corresponding sequence of actions at ∈ AGUI executed
                                                                            by the agent, where AGUI denotes the unified action space
                                                                            (e.g. coordinate-based taps, swipes, and text inputs).
                                                                          For task Tk , we define a training set Dktrain and a test set Dktest ,
                                                                          both composed of trajectories sampled from applications in
                                                                          Ak .

Figure 3. Overview of the proposed CGL framework. (Left) Error-Aware Routing pipeline:It dynamically routes data based on
prediction feedback, where erroneous actions trigger SFT knowledge injection to facilitate correction. (Top Right) Gradient Surgery:
Resolves directional conflicts between GRPO and SFT gradients through projection to maintain optimization stability. (Bottom Right)
Entropy-Regulated Tuning: A dynamic strategy that manages the exploration-exploitation trade-off by adjusting the SFT weight λ. The
bottom bar charts illustrate the model’s action probability distribution p, where the yellow shaded area denotes the ground truth (gt) action
range.

of rapidly emerging mobile applications and frequent soft-

ware updates, yet existing datasets lack dedicated bench-

marks tailored to dynamic GUI environments. To address
                                                                           Transportation (TT), System Tools (ST), Education and Sci-
this gap, we propose the AndroidControl-CL benchmark,
                                                                           ence (ES), and Life and Entertainment (LE). This design
an extension of AndroidControl [20] with additional anno-
                                                                           is motivated by the observation that apps within the same
tations and structured task splits. This benchmark is specif-
                                                                           super-class tend to exhibit similar task logic, UI layouts,
ically designed for the systematic evaluation of Continual

GUI Learning (CGL).

5.2. Entropy-Regulated Tuning                                          During collaborative training of Supervised Fine-Tuning
                                                                       (SFT) and GRPO (a reinforcement learning-based objec-
To manage the transition from exploration to exploitation

across sequential tasks, we introduce a dynamic weight-
                                                                       bilize optimization and impair knowledge preservation. To
ing factor λ(H, step) to modulate the contribution of SFT.

11.3. Comparison with Multi-Task Joint Training
We further compare our sequential learning approach
against the theoretical upper bound of Multi-Task Joint
Training (Tab. 13). Joint training assumes simultaneous ac-
cess to all datasets, which is typically impractical for dy-
namic, real-world GUI agents.
    Remarkably, CGL significantly narrows the gap be-
tween sequential learning and joint training. As illus-
trated in Tab. 13:
• The average trajectory accuracy of CGL across three dif-
   ferent task orders is 82.33% (Order 1), 82.61% (Order
   2), and 82.40% (Order 3).
• These results are highly competitive with the GRPO-
   Joint-Training baseline, which achieves 82.41%. No-
   tably, our method under Task Order 2 even slightly out-
   performs the GRPO joint training baseline.
• While SFT-Joint-Training reaches the highest abso-
   lute accuracy (83.48%), it requires full data accessibil-
   ity. CGL achieves comparable performance to the RL-
   based joint training upper bound while strictly adhering to
   the sequential learning constraint, validating the efficacy
   of our Entropy-Regulated Tuning and Gradient Surgery
   mechanisms in maintaining policy optimality over time.

sequence: (1) Launch the application via Open(Amazon); (2) Focus on the search field via Click(0.507, 0.089); (3) Input the
product query via Input text(‘‘Nike shoes’’); (4) Select the target suggestion via Click(0.444, 0.210); (5) Browse the
product list via Scroll(down); (6) Terminate the episode via Finish(). Coordinates indicate the relative (x, y) position on the screen
interface.

category via Input text(‘‘football gloves’’); (4) Select the top suggestion via Click(0.490, 0.152); (5) Terminate
the task via Finish().

Click(0.499, 0.603); (4) Initiate playback via Click(0.500, 0.203); (5) Terminate the task via Finish().
